name: NexJu AI – AI Chatbot & Website Assistant
author: nexjuai

sections.description:
NexJu AI is an AI chatbot for the websites of small businesses: it answers your visitors’ questions from what is on your website and takes requests for you.

What the assistant does for your visitors:

  • It answers questions about your services, prices and opening hours from the content of your website.
  • It takes requests and callback wishes and sends them to you by email.
  • It says openly that it is an AI assistant.
  • It answers in German and English, in the larger plans in your visitor’s language.
  • Your website only loads a small script of about 5 KB; the chat itself loads when a visitor opens it.

You set everything up right here in WordPress, without copying any code and without changing your theme. Under “Settings” → “NexJu AI” you sign in with your email address (we send you a code; with a new address your free account is created at the same time), the assistant reads your website, you check what it has learned, enter your company details and start for free. The plugin then installs the assistant by itself. Only paying for a paid plan happens on Stripe’s checkout page, in a new tab.

What the plugin does:

  • It loads the assistant’s script in the footer of every page.
  • It guides you through the setup step by step: industry, reading your website, checking the knowledge, company details and confirmations, free start or a paid plan.
  • Once the assistant runs, the settings page and a box in the dashboard show how it is doing: conversations this month and the number of new requests.
  • You can also connect on the NexJu AI website with one click, or paste the line of code by hand. The plugin only accepts the assistant of the account you signed in with, an assistant that comes back with the one-time value it created for you, or the line in exactly its form, and does not store any other code.
  • If you remove the assistant from your website (“Remove”, “Disconnect” or an empty line of code), the plugin does not install it again by itself; you install it again with one click.
  • It stores the assistant’s identifier and, after you sign in, an access key for this website. When you delete the plugin, both are removed and the plugin asks NexJu AI to revoke the key. If your account uses two-step sign-in, the plugin asks for the code from your authenticator app too.

What you need: an email address; the account at NexJu AI (nexjuai.com) is created during the setup if you do not have one yet. The assistant only runs on websites with HTTPS. The free plan includes 30 conversations once (not every month), without a payment method and without a minimum term. Paid plans start at €29 net per month. Accounts are only available to businesses based in Germany.

The plugin’s interface is available in English and German.

External services

The plugin embeds a script from app.nexjuai.com. This service is operated by JuNa Web UG (haftungsbeschränkt). When any page loads, the script and the assistant’s settings are fetched from there; like any web server, the service learns the visitor’s IP address and the address of the website. If a visitor writes in the assistant, their messages as well as the path and title of the page currently open are transmitted there and answered there. The assistant sets no cookies and stores nothing in the browser.

The plugin itself sends nothing anywhere until an administrator acts. For the setup on the settings page, the plugin sends requests from this WordPress server to https://app.nexjuai.com/api/wordpress/verbindung (never from your visitors’ browsers): the email address an administrator enters to sign in and the code from the email (and, with two-step sign-in, the code from the authenticator app); with every request the host name of this website and the language of the dashboard; the chosen industry; the knowledge texts checked and released there; the company details (only while none are stored in the account yet), the business email for requests and the confirmations entered there; the chosen plan and payment interval and the address of the plugin’s settings page (to return there after paying). When an administrator clicks “Read website”, the service fetches the public pages of this website itself, like a search engine. The service answers with the state of the setup: the email address of the account, the company details and the knowledge stored there (to show them for checking), and, once the assistant runs, its identifier, the number of conversations this month and the number of new requests (never the content of requests). After signing in, the plugin stores an access key for this website in the WordPress database (not loaded on other pages); the service only stores a hash of it. The plugin asks the service for the current state when an administrator opens the settings page or the dashboard (the dashboard box at most every ten minutes, after an error at most every three minutes); while the settings page stays open, also every five seconds while the website is being read and every ten seconds while the step for choosing a plan is open for the administrator who signed in, for at most ten minutes. “Sign out” revokes the key; deleting the plugin also asks the service to revoke it (if the service cannot be reached at that moment, disconnect the website in your account). A key that has not been used for 90 days expires. To pay for a paid plan, the plugin opens Stripe’s checkout page (checkout.stripe.com) in a new tab: https://stripe.com/legal and https://stripe.com/privacy.

Alternatively, when an administrator clicks “Connect with NexJu AI” under “Other ways”, the browser is sent to app.nexjuai.com with the address of this website, the address of the plugin’s settings page, a one-time value and the language of the dashboard; nothing else. app.nexjuai.com sends the browser back to the settings page with the identifier of the chosen assistant and the same one-time value.

  • Terms of service (German): https://app.nexjuai.com/recht/agb
  • Privacy policy of the service (German): https://app.nexjuai.com/recht/datenschutz
  • What data the assistant processes, in English: https://nexjuai.com/data
  • Privacy policy of the website nexjuai.com, in English: https://nexjuai.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. In the WordPress dashboard choose “Plugins” → “Add Plugin”, search for “NexJu AI” and click “Install Now”. (Or choose “Upload Plugin” and select the ZIP file from your account.)
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open “Settings” → “NexJu AI”.
  4. Enter your email address and the code from the email. Then follow the steps on the page: industry, read website, check knowledge, company details, start. At the end the assistant is installed.
  5. If you use a caching plugin, clear the cache once.
sections.faq:
What does it cost?

The free plan costs nothing: 30 conversations once, without a payment method and without a minimum term; one free assistant per business. It does not start again each month. The chat window shows “with NexJu AI”. When the 30 conversations are used up, new visitors get a short request form instead of the chat, their requests still reach you, and nothing is charged; for the assistant to answer again, choose a paid plan. For more conversations there are three plans: Start €29, Plus €59 or Profi €99 net per month plus 19 % VAT, cancellable monthly; on the annual plan €24, €49 or €82 per month with a 12-month minimum term. Included are 100, 250 or 600 conversations per month. The plugin itself is free. All prices: https://nexjuai.com/pricing

How do I start?

Open “Settings” → “NexJu AI” and sign in with your email address. Without an account it is created for free on the way. Then the page guides you: the assistant reads your website, you check what it has learned, enter your company details and start for free. At the end the assistant is installed.

Do I have to copy any code?

No. The setup on the settings page installs the assistant. If you prefer, you can connect on the NexJu AI website or paste the line of code from your account (“Code & installation”) under “Other ways”.

Connecting says the connection has expired.

This concerns the way under “Other ways”: click “Connect with NexJu AI” again, in the same browser. Or sign in on the settings page instead. If your WordPress dashboard runs without HTTPS or under a different address than your website, paste the line of code by hand instead: you find it in your account under “Code & installation”.

The assistant does not appear.

It only runs on the domain you set it up for, and only on websites with HTTPS. Also clear your website’s cache. In your account you can have it checked whether the line has arrived on your website.

Is the setup safe?

The plugin signs in with a code that only you receive by email (and, with two-step sign-in, a code from your app). After that it holds an access key that only works for this website and only for one assistant, the one of this website; it cannot see or change other assistants, invoices or the content of requests, and it cannot change company details that are already stored in your account. Only the administrator who signed in continues the setup; other administrators of the website see its state. Another administrator can sign out or sign in with their own account instead; this ends the previous sign-in on this website. Every new connection is announced to you by email, and in your account under “Settings” → “Sign-in and security” you see every connected WordPress website and can disconnect it.

Does the assistant set cookies?

No.

Does it work with my theme?

Yes, with any theme that outputs the standard WordPress footer. The plugin loads the script through WordPress itself.

Does it slow down my website?

Hardly: your pages load a script of about 5 KB. The chat itself only loads when a visitor opens it.

Which languages does the assistant speak?

German and English. In the larger plans it answers in your visitor’s language.
sections.changelog:
1.4.1

  • New name in the plugin directory: “NexJu AI – AI Chatbot & Website Assistant”. Nothing changes in how the plugin works.

1.4.0

  • Set up everything in WordPress: sign in with a code by email (also with two-step sign-in), choose the industry, read your website, check and release the knowledge, company details and confirmations, start for free or choose a paid plan. Only the payment opens Stripe in a new tab.
  • Once the assistant runs: conversations this month and new requests on the settings page and in a dashboard box.
  • Connecting on the NexJu AI website and the line of code by hand are still available under “Other ways”.
  • Security: an assistant you removed from your website is not installed again by itself; only the administrator who signed in continues the setup; deleting the plugin also asks NexJu AI to revoke the access key.
  • The free plan now includes 30 conversations once instead of every month; the settings page and the dashboard box show how many have been used.

1.3.0

  • Connect with one click: “Connect with NexJu AI” installs the assistant, without copying any code. The plugin only accepts an assistant that comes back with a one-time value it created for you.
  • “Disconnect” removes the assistant again.
  • The line of code can still be pasted by hand.

1.2.7

  • Settings page: without a line of code it shows the free plan and the prices, with a button to start for free.
  • Description: the free plan, the prices and two more questions and answers.

1.2.6

  • Description: what the assistant does, three more questions and answers. No change to the code.

1.2.5

  • Security hardening: the script tag is extended instead of replaced (attributes set by WordPress or other plugins stay), translations cannot break the settings page, an older saved address is rewritten once, and uninstalling in large networks runs in batches.

1.2.4

  • Description: NexJu AI is only available to businesses based in Germany. No change to the code.

1.2.3

  • The script is always loaded from app.nexjuai.com; lines of code with the older address keep working.
  • A damaged setting in the database no longer stops the site.

1.2.2

  • Only the address of the service’s own script is accepted in the line of code.
  • On a network (multisite), deleting the plugin removes the setting on every site.

1.2.1

  • German translations follow the WordPress glossary and use the informal or the formal form, as WordPress itself does.

1.2.0

  • The colours of the settings page are loaded as a stylesheet file.
  • Links to the terms and the privacy policy of the service in this readme.

1.1.0

  • Interface in English and German.
  • Settings page in the colours of NexJu AI.

1.0.0

  • First version.
